I own products from the first client call to the release: the data model, the Flutter app, the TypeScript backend and the deploy. At **Value Digital Services** I build banking, insurance and HR apps for the BIAT group and its clients. As an independent engineer I build event platforms, booking agents and data pipelines for clients in Tunisia, France and Dubai.

Most of that code is private client work. The numbers above count it, and the sections below describe it.

## How I ship

<picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/ship-dark.svg"><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/ship-light.svg"><img alt="Diagram of the loop behind every feature, in five steps. 01 Grill: Question the request until nothing is ambiguous. 02 Spec: PRD with testable EARS acceptance criteria. 03 Build: Parallel agent panes, split along the code's natural seams. 04 Review: Effort sized to the diff, plus a second model as a gate. 05 Ship: Green by exit code, never by a model's opinion. After review, a fix loop returns to build until the gate is green. A human signs off at steps 01 and 05. Tools I wrote for this loop: assay (public) · cmax · mate · fob · figma-fidelity." src="assets/ship-light.svg" width="100%"></picture>

I use coding agents every day, and I treat their output like a pull request from a new teammate: specified first, reviewed twice, merged only when the checks pass. The public version of this loop is [assay, a Claude Code skill](https://github.com/HabibPro1999/assay).
